lines: Six gate inputs feed six logic operations; each operation that is high adds one of three tunable intervals to a pitch, and three voices read that pitch while ignoring inputs of their own choosing
Up includes that input in this column's logic operation, the middle position leaves it out, and down includes it inverted, so a low gate counts as high
Chooses the logic operation for this column: OR, &, XOR, >=2, Maj or Off, reading only the inputs whose switches in the column are up or down
Sends this column's gate to the Top, Middle or Bottom interval; each time the column is high, that interval is added once more to the pitch
Chooses the interval this row contributes: OFF, 8va, P5, M3, P4, m3, M2, m2, 7/4, 11/8, 13/8 or 31/16, tuned as exact frequency ratios rather than equal-tempered steps
Unlit, this voice ignores that input: the matrix is worked out at every combination of the ignored inputs and the pitches sorted for Pitch Select to choose from; lit, the input is used as it stands
Picks which of the pitches the co-muted inputs produce this voice takes, the lowest at full counter-clockwise and the highest at full clockwise
Gate input A; with nothing patched it stays low, because there is no input above it to divide
A gate input, reading high above 1V and low below 0V; with nothing patched it runs at half the rate of the nearest patched input above, so one clock at A cascades down the column
Adds to that voice's Pitch Select knob at a fifth of the knob's range per volt, so 0V to 5V covers it; a polyphonic cable here makes that voice's two outputs polyphonic
Adds to the interval that row contributes, a volt per octave, so the knob can be left at OFF and the interval taken entirely from here
A trigger here resets the divide-by-two counters of the unpatched inputs, each taking effect the next time the input above it goes high
With a cable here the module works out a new step only on a pulse at this input, which steadies it when gates arrive on slightly different frames
5V while this column's logic operation is high and 0V otherwise, untouched by the interval and co-mute settings
That voice's pitch, a volt per octave, summed from the intervals that the high operations contribute
A 5V pulse 10ms long each time that voice's pitch changes
Note — patch one clock to input A and the five inputs below it divide by two in turn, which gives a 64-step cycle to work from; without that, or gates of your own, nothing moves
Note — the intervals are exact frequency ratios and stack as fractions, so pitches drift away from the keyboard; the 12 EDO Mode menu item rounds each interval to the nearest semitone instead
Note — the light beside each input jack shows that input high, the light under each Logic Out shows that operation high, and the light by each Trig output flashes when the voice changes
Note — LatticeExpander placed immediately to the right shows which notes the voices are landing on
Menu — Randomize Matrix — sets the matrix switches at random; a submenu offers Level 0, Level 1 and Level 2, from tame to wild
Menu — Randomize Intervals — sets the three interval knobs at random; a submenu offers Level 0, Level 1 and Level 2, from tame to wild
Menu — Randomize CoMutes — sets the co-mute buttons at random; a submenu offers Level 0, Level 1 and Level 2, from tame to wild
Menu — Randomize Percentiles — sets the three Pitch Select knobs at random
Menu — Randomize All — sets the matrix, intervals, co-mutes and Pitch Select knobs at random together; a submenu offers Level 0, Level 1 and Level 2
Menu — 12 EDO Mode — rounds each interval, knob and CV added together, to the nearest twelfth of an octave
Menu — Time Quantize Mode — reads the switches and knobs only when an input gate or a Pitch Select CV changes, so a change made by hand lands on the next step rather than mid-step

LameJuis.notes: Read at commit debdfae, 'bump version to 2.1.0', whose res/LameJuis.svg is byte-identical to the installed panel; later commits keep the version at 2.1.0 while the repository moves off Rack entirely. The manual says the randomizers offer levels 0 to 3; LameJuisModel.cpp loops level < 3, so the submenus print Level 0, Level 1 and Level 2. The manual also says the video tutorial predates a panel transpose, so rows in the video are columns on this panel. The maker's tooltips call the six logic columns 'Step 1' to 'Step 6' while the panel prints S1 to S6, and call the co-mute positions 'Co-Muted' and 'On' where the panel gives no position names. Every parameter, input and output has a widget, so all 72 controls are reachable. The interval CV is coloured pitch because it is added in octaves to a pitch and the maker documents feeding a microtonal quantizer into it; the pitch select CV is coloured cv because its 0V to 5V span is an index into a sorted list rather than a pitch.

lines: A grid of lights and note names showing where on the lattice of whole-number frequency ratios LameJuis is currently playing
Note — it has no jacks and no controls; place it immediately to the right of LameJuis, the only module it reads, and it goes dark beside anything else
Note — the horizontal axis counts the Top interval and the vertical axis the Middle interval; the Bottom interval moves between planes of the lattice
Note — only one plane is drawn at a time, the one holding the most voices, and the lowest wins a tie, so a voice on another plane shows nothing
Note — voice 1 lights red, voice 2 green and voice 3 blue, and a polyphonic voice lights one square per channel
Note — the squares are named as notes while all three intervals are the familiar ones and no interval CV is patched; otherwise they are labelled in cents
LatticeExpander.notes: The module declares no parameters, inputs or outputs at all, so nothing on it can be clicked for help except the title band. The note names are drawn in LedDisplayTextField widgets whose text is rewritten from the module every frame, so typing into one does not stick.
